biography.value:
Biography of Wario in This Timeline

In this alternate, war-torn Mushroom Kingdom timeline—set amid the aftermath of Princess Peach's assassination in 955 BF and the subsequent prolonged civil war—Wario emerges as the quintessential opportunistic wildcard, a greedy chaos agent who thrives in the power vacuum left by fractured kingdoms and collapsing allegiances. Where heroes seek justice and villains pursue conquest, Wario simply follows the money, laughing his distinctive "Wah ha ha!" while the world burns around him.

Physical Appearance & Core Traits

Wario remains instantly recognizable as Mario's burly, inverted counterpart: massively built with a physique that combines obesity with surprising muscular power, sporting a huge head, prominent jutting chin, oversized pink triangular nose, and wild zigzag mustache that twitches when he's plotting something profitable. His signature outfit never varies—yellow cap emblazoned with a prominent purple "W", purple overalls over a long-sleeved yellow shirt, green pointed shoes, and white gloves marked with blue "W"s on the backs.

His personality is equally consistent: hot-tempered, boisterous, crude, and utterly shameless in his greed. He thinks nothing of betraying allies, exploiting disasters, or causing collateral damage if there's profit in it. Unlike more ideologically-driven villains, Wario has no grand vision for the Mushroom Kingdom—he just wants to be rich, and he doesn't particularly care whose gold he's counting or whose burning city he's looting to get it.

Role in the Civil War Era (955 BF - Present)

Wario operates as a mercenary-treasure hunter-smuggler-pirate hybrid who drifts between factions with zero loyalty. He's worked temporary contracts for the Iron Legion when they paid well, sold intelligence to Peach Loyalists when the price was right, smuggled goods for Fawful's remnant forces, and double-crossed all of them when a better deal emerged. No faction trusts him, but many employ him because he's effective when properly motivated (i.e., paid in advance).

His operation includes a loose network of agents, muscle-for-hire, and disposable recruits. Key among these is "Wally," a mysterious operative who executed the dramatic extraction of Bowser during the chaotic Aftermath on the Vigilance events around Highsun 7, 1040 BF. Whether Wally is truly loyal to Wario or simply the highest bidder remains unclear—probably the latter.

Wario maintains no fixed base of operations, preferring to move between safehouses, smuggler ports, and temporary camps. He's been spotted in Iron Legion territories, Regal Empire border towns, the lawless Darklands, and even popping up in supernatural hotspots when ancient treasure is rumored to be involved. His ability to appear and disappear seemingly at will has led to speculation that he has access to Warp Pipes, airship networks, or dimensional shortcuts that he's keeping to himself.

Notable Activities & Incidents

The Vigilance Barrel Incident (Highsun 11, 1040 BF): During a massive brawl aboard the airship Vigilance—which doubled as a trafficking operation reveal—Wario was discovered hiding in a barrel amid the chaos, apparently waiting for everyone to finish killing each other so he could loot the bodies and cargo. When discovered, he fought his way out, stole several crates of unknown contents, and escaped via emergency Warp Pipe he'd apparently planted beforehand "just in case."

The Remi Recruitment (Highsun 12, 1040 BF): In one of his most characteristically cruel moves, Wario approached FNG Remi and presented her with what appeared to be a gift—a beautifully wrapped box. When she opened it, the bomb inside detonated, leaving her severely injured. As she lay bleeding, Wario laughed, tossed her a healing potion (which he charged to her account), and casually offered her a position in his crew. "You survived! That means you're tough! Wah ha ha! You're hired!" Whether Remi accepted or told him where to shove his job offer is unclear, but the incident perfectly encapsulates Wario's approach to recruitment: explosively terrible and entirely transactional.

Raventree Manor Operations (Highsun 16-22, 1040 BF): Wario inserted himself into the dimensional nightmare unfolding at Raventree Manor, claiming to be working with the Iron Legion to investigate temporal instabilities (a lie—he was there for rumored ancient treasure). During the looping dinner raid involving mirror dimensions, Oracles, vampires, hags, and the Orange Heir succession crisis, Wario set up increasingly bizarre schemes:

  • In a Feywild-adjacent fairy village manifestation within the manor's fractured reality, Wario dramatically unfurled an absurdly long wish-list containing 2,361 items, ranging from mundane supplies to reality-bending artifacts. He priced a legendary Star Rod at "900 trillion gold pieces, non-negotiable."
  • He successfully extracted payment in the form of abstract "experience" from a confused entity named hjumpik, though what this transaction actually accomplished remains metaphysically unclear.
  • He departed the fairy village with piles of ridiculous artifacts, including: seventeen cursed monkey paws ("they're collectibles!"), a mirror that shows only alternate timeline versions of yourself, three bags of "definitely not stolen" Koopa Troopa shells, and what he claimed was "the original recipe for Peach's cake" (authentication disputed).

Throughout the manor's escalating disasters—convergence rituals, planar fractures, vampire politics, Shadowfell bleed, and the succession war between Orangus Cornelius and various heirs—Wario remained focused exclusively on personal profit rather than any ideological position. He sold information to multiple parties, looted during dimensional breaches, and at one point tried to auction off a "genuine piece of the Dark Moon" (later revealed to be painted glass).

Current Status & Operations (1040 BF)

Wario continues to operate as a freelance chaos profiteer, appearing wherever the war creates opportunities for wealth extraction. Recent intelligence suggests he's involved in:

  • Smuggling operations moving restricted goods between Iron Legion and Regal Empire territories, charging exorbitant fees to both sides
  • Treasure hunting in war-torn ruins, with particular interest in pre-war Mushroom Kingdom vaults and abandoned castles
  • Arms dealing, selling weapons to whoever pays—he's been linked to shipments reaching Toad resistance cells, Bowser loyalists, and independent warlords
  • Running underground gambling operations in neutral zones, rigging the games whenever possible
  • Participating in airship hijackings, both as perpetrator and opportunistic "rescue" operator who charges victims for extraction

He has no known permanent allies, though he maintains working relationships with various criminals, smugglers, and mercenaries who share his profit-first philosophy. His relationship with Waluigi (his frequent partner in canonical timelines) is strained in this darker world—reports suggest they've had several violent falling-outs over split percentages, though they still occasionally collaborate when a job is too big for one greedy bastard to handle alone.

Combat Capabilities & Tactics

Despite his comical appearance and greedy motivations, Wario is genuinely dangerous in combat. His massive strength allows him to wield oversized weapons and grapple opponents much larger than himself. He fights dirty—eye gouges, groin strikes, thrown improvised weapons, and tactical retreats when outmatched are all standard in his playbook.

His signature moves include devastating shoulder charges that can knock enemies off airships or through walls, ground pounds that create shockwaves, and an inexplicable ability to eat almost anything and convert it into usable power (he's been documented eating bombs and turning them into explosive farts, which is horrifying but tactically effective).

Wario is cowardly when the odds aren't in his favor, readily fleeing combat if victory looks expensive or unlikely. However, when cornered or when protecting a significant treasure haul, he becomes ferociously aggressive, fighting with the desperate strength of someone who refuses to give up his gold without taking several enemies with him.

Personality Summary

Wario is greed incarnate, a living embodiment of avarice without the sophistication or long-term planning that characterizes more traditional villains. He wants money NOW, he wants ALL of it, and he'll laugh while taking it from whoever has it. He's cruel but not sadistic for its own sake—he'll blow up Remi because it's funny and establishes dominance, then hire her because capable muscle is profitable. He'll hide in a barrel during a battle because why risk injury when you can wait and loot the winners?

He has absolutely no sense of shame, honor, or loyalty beyond contractual obligations (and even those are negotiable if the breach is profitable enough). He's loud, obnoxious, and makes his signature "Wah ha ha!" laugh in situations where any sensible person would show restraint. He views the entire civil war as his personal treasure vault—a chaotic environment where traditional law and order have broken down, creating infinite opportunities for a sufficiently greedy and shameless opportunist.

Yet despite all this, he's not entirely stupid. He knows when to cut losses, when to hide, and when to run. He's survived eighty-five years of civil war not through idealism or military genius, but through pure mercenary pragmatism: if it's not profitable, don't do it. If it might get you killed, charge triple. If everyone else is dying, hide in a barrel and loot them afterward.

In a world of grand causes and terrible sacrifices, Wario remains committed to the only cause that's ever mattered to him: getting paid. Wah ha ha!

description.value: You make three attacks: two with your fists or weapons, and one shoulder charge or ground pound.
description.chat: You unleash a flurry of brutal strikes, combining raw strength with opportunistic violence in a display that's as effective as it is crude.

description.value: You deliver a devastating haymaker punch powered by your massive strength and complete disregard for fighting fair. The blow carries enough force to send opponents flying backward, and you're not above adding a headbutt or elbow strike if they're still standing after the initial impact. On a critical hit, the target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone as you literally punch them off their feet.
description.chat: You wind up with exaggerated theatrical motion, then unleash a brutal haymaker that connects with a meaty THWACK, your target's head snapping back from the impact of your massive fist.

description.value: You lower your shoulder and charge forward in a straight line up to 30 feet, building momentum with each step until you slam into your target with the force of a battering ram. This reckless charge allows you to move through spaces occupied by creatures of your size or smaller (they must make a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked aside 5 feet). When you hit a target with this charge, they take damage and must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone and pushed back 10 feet. If they're pushed into a wall, object, or another creature, they take an additional 2d6 bludgeoning damage from the impact. You can use this charge to break through wooden doors, barricades, or similar obstacles, treating them as having AC 10 and 20 hit points.
description.chat: You break into a dead sprint, building terrifying momentum as your heavy frame barrels forward. At the last second you lower your shoulder and SLAM into your target like a runaway minecart, the impact creating a visible shockwave as bodies go flying.

description.value: You leap into the air (up to 10 feet high if you have room) and come crashing down buttocks-first with devastating force, creating a shockwave upon impact. All creatures within 10 feet of your landing point must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take 4d6 bludgeoning damage and are knocked prone as the ground buckles beneath them. On a successful save, they take half damage and remain standing. The impact creates difficult terrain in a 10-foot radius as the ground cracks and splinters. If used on a wooden floor, airship deck, or similarly fragile surface, you may break through entirely (DM's discretion), which is sometimes intentional when you're trying to escape or cause maximum chaos.
description.chat: You leap into the air with surprising height for someone of your bulk, then plummet downward in a sitting position. The impact as you hit the ground is CATASTROPHIC—a visible shockwave radiates outward, cracks spiderweb across the floor, and everyone nearby is thrown off their feet by the tremor. "WAH HA HA!" you bellow, clearly pleased with the destruction.

description.value:
As an action, you can summon your signature purple motorcycle—the Wario Bike—which appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet in a cloud of exhaust smoke and the roar of an engine that's somehow both poorly maintained and indestructible. The bike functions as a mount with the following statistics: AC 14, 50 HP, speed 60 feet. While riding the bike, you can make ramming attacks (treat as Shoulder Charge but with an additional 1d8 bludgeoning damage) and have advantage on checks to maintain control during high-speed chases or dangerous maneuvers.

The bike runs on a mysterious fuel source (some say garlic oil, others suspect pure greed) and never seems to actually run out of gas despite Wario never refueling it. The bike can be dismissed as a bonus action, vanishing in another cloud of exhaust, or it disappears automatically if reduced to 0 HP (it can be resummoned after a long rest, emerging dented and smoking but functional).

The Wario Bike is loud, obnoxious, and produces enough pollution to violate every environmental regulation ever written. It also has a horn that plays a jarring "WAH HA HA HA!" when honked, which Wario uses constantly and inappropriately. The bike has been banned from at least seven cities for noise violations, emissions standards breaches, and "general obnoxiousness."
description.chat: You whistle sharply and your purple motorcycle roars into existence in a cloud of black exhaust smoke, skidding to a stop beside you with the screech of worn brakes. You swing your leg over the seat, rev the engine unnecessarily loud, and honk the horn, which blares "WAH HA HA HA!" across the battlefield. Everyone within earshot grimaces. You couldn't be more pleased.

description.value:
You can eat almost anything—and you do, because Wario's appetite is both legendary and horrifying. As a bonus action, you can attempt to bite and swallow a Small or smaller object, consumable, or even certain creatures (DM's discretion). This includes bombs (which you convert into explosive gas), potions (gaining their effects), coins (healing 1d4 HP per 10 gold pieces consumed, you sick bastard), and small enemies (dealing 2d6 + 5 piercing damage, and if this reduces them to 0 HP, you swallow them whole and gain temporary HP equal to their remaining HP).

Special interactions: If you eat a bomb or explosive device, you can use your reaction on your next turn to release it as a devastating fart in a 15-foot cone (DC 16 Constitution save, 3d6 fire damage and poisoned condition for 1 minute on failed save, half damage and no condition on success). This is absolutely disgusting but tactically effective.

You have advantage on saving throws against ingested poisons because your digestive system has adapted to process literally anything, including substances that would kill normal humans. Your stomach has become a garbage disposal of legendary efficiency and questionable biology.
description.chat: You open your mouth impossibly wide—far wider than human anatomy should allow—and CHOMP down on your target with the enthusiasm of someone who's never met a food safety regulation they couldn't violate. The sound of your chewing is audible across the battlefield and deeply unsettling to everyone present.

description.value:
Passive Ability. Your overwhelming greed provides tangible mechanical benefits, because apparently avarice is a superpower in your world. You have advantage on all Wisdom (Perception) checks to notice treasure, valuables, hidden wealth, or anything worth money. You can smell gold within 60 feet (literally—you have developed a supernatural sense for currency), and you instinctively know the approximate value of any object you can see within 30 feet.

Additionally, whenever you see someone carrying visible wealth (coins, jewelry, magic items worth 100gp or more), you must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or become fixated on acquiring it, gaining advantage on attacks against that creature but having disadvantage on attacks against any other target until you either take the wealth or the wealthy creature leaves your sight.

Finally, you can use your gold as a resource in desperate situations: by spending 100gp worth of coins as a bonus action, you heal yourself for 2d8 + 5 HP as your greed literally sustains you. The coins vanish into your body (you eat them), and you feel warm satisfaction wash over you. "Money IS happiness! WAH HA HA!"
description.chat: Your eyes literally transform into gold coin symbols as you spot something valuable, a cartoonish but genuine physiological response to the presence of wealth. You begin gravitating toward it unconsciously, fingers twitching with acquisitive hunger.

description.value:
Passive and Reaction Ability. You have no shame about running away when a fight turns against you—in fact, you've turned cowardice into an art form. When you take the Dash or Disengage action, your movement speed increases by 10 feet as pure fear and greed fuel your escape. Additionally, you have advantage on all Dexterity saving throws made to avoid area effects (fireballs, exploding barrels, collapsing floors) because your self-preservation instinct is finely honed.

As a reaction when you would be hit by an attack, you can attempt to grab a nearby creature of your size or smaller and use them as a human shield. Make a contested Strength (Athletics) check against the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). On a success, the attack hits them instead of you, and you shove them 5 feet away afterward. "WAH! Not me, HIM!"

Finally, if you are reduced to 0 hit points while you have at least 100gp worth of treasure on your person, you can spend all of your carried wealth as a reaction to instead drop to 1 hit point and immediately teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see as your emergency Warp Pipe activates (you always keep one hidden on your person for exactly this situation). You emerge from the teleportation prone, gasping, and broke—but alive, which is what matters.
description.chat: The moment things turn against you, your survival instincts kick into overdrive. Your eyes widen, you emit a panicked "WAHHH!", and you're suddenly moving with speed that seems physically impossible for someone of your bulk, trampling allies and enemies alike in your desperate flight toward safety and profit preservation.

description.value:
Rare Vehicle. Your heavily modified purple motorcycle, customized with weapons, armor plating, and enough illegal modifications to get you arrested in any civilized territory. The bike serves as both transportation and mobile weapons platform, perfect for drive-by looting and high-speed escapes.

Statistics: AC 16 (reinforced frame with spiked armor plating), 75 HP, Speed 70 feet, can carry up to 500 pounds of cargo in saddlebags and hidden compartments (where you keep emergency gold and stolen goods). The bike can traverse difficult terrain without speed penalty and can make jumps up to 30 feet long with a running start.

Mounted Weapons: The bike features a forward-facing flamethrower (bonus action to activate, 15-foot cone, DC 14 Dexterity save, 2d6 fire damage), spiked wheel guards (creatures hit by ramming attacks take an extra 1d6 piercing damage), and an oil slick dispenser (action to activate, creates 30-foot line of difficult terrain behind you that lasts 1 minute, creatures entering must make DC 14 Dexterity save or fall prone).

The bike runs on "Wario Fuel"—a proprietary blend that smells like garlic, burns purple, and is probably illegal in most jurisdictions. You've never actually bought fuel for it; you just sort of... will it to keep running through sheer greed and stubbornness, and somehow it works.

The bike is also equipped with: hidden storage compartments (total capacity 50 cubic feet for smuggling), a mounted horn that plays your signature laugh, spiked handlebars for close-combat situations, and a license plate that reads "WAHAHA" (the plate is from a kingdom that no longer exists, making it technically untraceable).
description.chat: You rev the engine on your custom chopper and the purple beast roars to life, belching black smoke from its exhaust pipes. The spikes on the wheel guards gleam menacingly, the flamethrower attachment hums as it warms up, and the entire machine vibrates with barely-contained mechanical violence. You pat the fuel tank affectionately. "Good bike. Let's go make some money."

unidentified.name: Modified Purple Motorcycle
unidentified.description: A heavily customized purple motorcycle that looks like it was designed by someone with more money than taste and a deep love of violence. The bike features spiked armor plating, what appears to be a flamethrower mounted to the front, and numerous compartments of unclear purpose. The exhaust pipes are modified to be unnecessarily loud, and the whole thing radiates "illegal modifications." The license plate reads "WAHAHA."

description.value:
Legendary Item (Unique). An impossibly long scroll that unfurls to reveal 2,361 individually itemized wishes, demands, and desired acquisitions compiled by Wario over the course of his treasure-hunting career. The scroll itself is approximately 847 feet long when fully extended, written in Wario's barely-legible scrawl with occasional crude drawings of the items in question.

The list ranges from the mundane ("47 wheels of fancy cheese", "new purple overalls, the expensive kind") to the absurd ("a castle, but not a haunted one this time", "seventeen cursed monkey paws for my collection") to the cosmically expensive ("Star Rod - 900 trillion gold pieces NON-NEGOTIABLE" is written in all caps with multiple underlines).

Notable entries include: every coin in the Mushroom Kingdom, a working Warp Pipe network for personal use, Princess Peach's castle ("she's not using it anymore"), Bowser's gold reserves, a lifetime supply of garlic, the original recipe for Peach's cake, a mirror that shows only alternate timeline versions of yourself, three bags of "definitely not stolen" Koopa Troopa shells, and something cryptically listed as "that thing Waluigi has that he KNOWS I want."

Recent additions to the list include items looted or desired from Raventree Manor: "vampire wine cellars (all of them)", "the Orange Heir's inheritance documents (for blackmail purposes)", "whatever the hags are hiding in the Shadowfell basement", "that weird Oracle's prediction book", and "enough Feywild fairy dust to retire on."

The scroll has been used in bizarre metaphysical transactions, most notably when Wario successfully extracted payment in the form of abstract "experience" from an entity named hjumpik during the Feywild manifestation at Raventree Manor. How this transaction worked, what experience actually means in this context, and whether hjumpik understood what they were agreeing to remains unclear. Wario insists it was a "fair deal" and that hjumpik "got what they paid for," though he's conspicuously vague about what that actually was.

The wish-list serves no mechanical combat purpose, but it's invaluable for understanding Wario's priorities (everything), his negotiating positions (unreasonable), and his long-term goals (acquire literally all wealth in existence, then maybe get lunch). Enemies who've seen the list describe it as "simultaneously pathetic and terrifying" because it reveals a mind that has genuinely, seriously considered how to steal every valuable object in the known world.
description.chat: You dramatically unfurl the scroll with a theatrical flourish, and it keeps unfurling... and unfurling... and unfurling. Within seconds, the scroll has covered the floor in multiple overlapping loops, creating a maze of parchment that everyone has to step over. You clear your throat importantly and begin reading: "Item number one: Every coin currently in circulation in the Mushroom Kingdom..." This is going to take a while.

unidentified.name: Extremely Long Scroll
unidentified.description: A scroll case that seems to contain far more parchment than should physically fit inside. When opened, the scroll extends to truly absurd lengths, covered in cramped handwriting and crude sketches. The sheer amount of text suggests this is either a historical chronicle, a legal document of Byzantine complexity, or someone's extremely detailed shopping list.

description.value:
Rare Consumable. A compact, collapsible Warp Pipe that Wario keeps hidden on his person at all times for emergency escapes. When activated as a bonus action, the pipe rapidly expands to full size (a green pipe approximately 4 feet tall), and you can immediately use it to teleport up to 1 mile to any location you've previously visited. The pipe remains active for 1 round, during which other creatures can also use it (though Wario typically activates it and jumps in before anyone else can react).

After use, the pipe collapses back into its compact form but becomes inert—it's a one-time-use device that requires expensive recalibration and charging at a Warp Pipe hub to function again. Wario keeps several of these stashed in various safehouses, but he's extremely protective of them because they represent his ultimate escape plan when a job goes catastrophically wrong.

The pipe's destination is set when it's calibrated, and Wario typically programs his to lead to his most secure vault or a neutral-territory black market where he can disappear into the criminal underground. Smart enemies who've fought Wario before know to watch for the telltale green glow of an activating emergency pipe—it means he's about to vanish with whatever he's stolen, and you have approximately 3 seconds to stop him before he's gone.

The pipes are manufactured by an underground network of Toad engineers who've made a fortune selling emergency teleportation devices to criminals, smugglers, and mercenaries. Wario has a standing order for ten pipes per month, which he goes through with alarming regularity given how often his schemes go sideways and require desperate escapes.
description.chat: You slap the compact cylinder against the ground and it EXPLODES outward into a full-sized green Warp Pipe with a distinctive *bwooomp* sound. Without hesitation, you dive headfirst into the pipe, your legs kicking comically in the air for a moment before you're sucked down and away with a whooshing sound. The pipe collapses behind you with a *pop*, leaving nothing but faint green sparkles and the distant echo of your mocking laughter.

unidentified.name: Collapsible Green Cylinder
unidentified.description: A compact metallic cylinder, bright green with yellow trim, covered in warning labels in multiple languages. It appears to be some kind of emergency device—there's a large red activation button on one end and what looks like dimensional runes etched into the surface. Handle with extreme caution.

description.value:
Uncommon Consumable (Weapon). A beautifully wrapped present box, complete with elaborate bow and festive paper, that contains a primed Bob-omb set to detonate when the box is opened. This is Wario's idea of a "gift," typically given to people he wants to recruit (after testing their durability) or enemies he wants to eliminate (while laughing about their trust issues).

When the box is opened, the Bob-omb inside explodes immediately. The creature opening the box and all creatures within 10 feet must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, creatures take 6d6 fire damage and are knocked prone. On a successful save, they take half damage and remain standing. The explosion destroys the box entirely and leaves scorch marks in a 10-foot radius.

Wario keeps several of these prepared at all times, storing them in his Bag of Holding (which is concerning—one accidental detonation inside the extradimensional space could cause catastrophic damage, but Wario insists "it'll be fine, probably"). He's been known to leave them as "traps" in locations he's looted, give them to people he's negotiating with to establish dominance, or throw them as improvised grenades when he can't be bothered to unwrap them first.

The most infamous use of the Bomb Gift Box was when Wario gave one to FNG Remi on Highsun 12, 1040 BF. After it exploded and nearly killed her, he offered her a healing potion (at cost) and a job, reasoning that anyone who survived his recruitment test was tough enough to be useful. Whether this says more about Wario's cruelty or his pragmatic approach to hiring is a matter of ongoing debate.

The wrapping paper is actually quite nice—Wario pays extra for quality presentation because "if you're going to blow someone up, you should at least have the courtesy to make it look festive." He has a Toad in one of the black markets who specializes in gift-wrapping explosives, and Wario is their best customer.
description.chat: You present the beautifully wrapped box with both hands, a huge grin on your face that doesn't quite reach your eyes. "For you! A gift! Go on, open it!" you encourage enthusiastically, already taking several steps backward in anticipation of the imminent explosion. Your fingers are in your ears before the recipient even touches the ribbon. You're giggling.

unidentified.name: Wrapped Gift Box
unidentified.description: A present box wrapped in festive paper with an elaborate bow. It's surprisingly heavy for its size, and you can hear something faintly ticking inside. The wrapping job is actually quite nice—someone put effort into making this look appealing, which makes the suspicious weight and ticking sound all the more concerning.
